evidence: 'They Reminisce Over You (T.R.O.Y.)' (1992), produced by Pete Rock, samples parts of the saxophone solo in Tom Scott and the California Dreamers' 'Today' from The Honeysuckle Breeze (Impulse!, 1967), as recorded in the song's sample credits.

earlier.artist: Tom Scott and the California Dreamers
earlier.title: Today

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Wait for Scott's saxophone solo in 'Today', then listen to 'T.R.O.Y.'. Pete Rock has taken pieces of that solo and turned them into a short, repeating horn line, the melody everyone remembers. A soft 1967 version of a Jefferson Airplane song has become a memorial for a friend who died. The notes are Scott's. The grief is Pete Rock's.

explanation.age7: Pete Rock took a few notes of saxophone from an old jazz song to make 'T.R.O.Y.'.
explanation.age13: Tom Scott recorded 'Today', a jazz version of a Jefferson Airplane song, in 1967 when he was a teenager. Pete Rock took parts of its saxophone solo and looped them into the main tune of 'T.R.O.Y.', his song remembering his friend Troy Dixon.
